messages:
Anika Patel: Quick design check — folks, I pushed the new mock for the Usage dashboard into Figma. Main question: do we default to Org-level or Project-level when users first land? Current mock shows Org by default with a prominent "Overview" card and a smaller "Project quick switch" on the right.
Jamie Chen: I'm leaning project-first for new signups (they usually start with one project). For org admins, a persistent toggle at top could remember last choice.
Matt O'Neill: Agree with Jamie. Can we make the toggle keyboard-focusable? i.e. tab -> space toggles and aria-pressed.
Sarah Lopez: +1 on keyboard focus. Also accessibility note: ensure the chart legend has clear labels, not just color swatches — screen readers need text.
Anika Patel: Good call. Proposal: initial view = Project for new orgs, fall back to Org for users with >1 project. Persist choice in profile. Thoughts on where to surface the invoice link? Top-right global nav vs inside the Billing card?
Jamie Chen: Put Download invoice in two places: small link in the Billing card and global Action menu (three dots). Helps discoverability without cluttering header.
Matt O'Neill: If we duplicate the link, let's make the global one the canonical link and the card one a shortcut with aria-describedby pointing to it.
Sarah Lopez: Microcopy nit: on the token breakdown tooltip we currently say "Tokens used (approx)" — that's ambiguous. Suggest: "Estimated tokens consumed — includes prompts + responses; billing uses rounded token counts." Shorter: "Estimated tokens (billing rounded)."
Anika Patel: Good microcopy. Can someone draft the exact string for design?
Jamie Chen: How about: "Estimated tokens consumed (rounded for billing)."
Matt O'Neill: I prefer: "Estimated tokens — includes prompt + response; billing rounds counts." Keeps the clause.
Sarah Lopez: For mobile collapse behavior: the stacked bar chart should become a simple sparklines list with per-project totals. Avoid tiny tappable legend items.
Anika Patel: UX question: chart style — stacked vs grouped for multi-project views. Stacked shows total at a glance, grouped makes per-project comparison easier. Which should be default?
Jamie Chen: Use stacked by default, with a "Compare projects" toggle that switches to grouped. Default stacked better for cost-signal.
Matt O'Neill: Implementation note: when switching to grouped, change the y-axis scale to per-project max, and show a subtle animation. Keep series order consistent to avoid color confusion.
Sarah Lopez: Accessibility: color alone can't convey project identity. Add pattern fills for high-contrast mode and ensure legend entries contain project names in text.
Anika Patel: Agree. Also a11y: keyboard shortcut to toggle between Overview/Projects (maybe "g o" for go overview?). Too fancy?
Jamie Chen: Might be overkill for now. Let's prioritize focus order and skip custom shortcuts this round.
Matt O'Neill: Small code suggestion for the toggle to satisfy a11y:
```html
<button aria-pressed="false" aria-controls="usage-panel" id="view-toggle">Project view</button>
```
And update aria-pressed on toggle.
Sarah Lopez: For the invoices table accessibility: add role="table" and ensure each header has scope="col" and data-col-name attributes for CSV export mapping. Also add a visible focus ring for keyboard nav.
Anika Patel: CSV & export UX — do we want token-level export (per-call rows) or just aggregated daily totals? Customers asked for both historically.
Jamie Chen: Start with aggregated daily totals and a "Request raw exports" link for heavy users. We can gate raw exports behind a permission/role.
Matt O'Neill: Agree. For performance, generate raw exports async and email a link. Add a toast: "Raw export requested — we’ll email you when ready."
Sarah Lopez: Copy for the export button: "Export CSV — daily totals" and a secondary action: "Request raw call log". Add aria-labels: "Export CSV of daily totals".
Anika Patel: One last visual: the cost breakdown card currently uses pie + table. Designer suggests replacing pie with a horizontal bar list (better accessibility). Thoughts?
Jamie Chen: Horizontal bars are easier to read and label-aligned. Pie charts are hard for comparisons and inaccessible for screen readers. Replace pie.
Matt O'Neill: Yes please replace pie with bars. Keep an accessible summary sentence above the visual for SR users: e.g., "Top contributors to cost: Project A 42%, Project B 31%, Other 27%."
Sarah Lopez: Love that. Also ensure color contrast passes WCAG 4.5:1 for small text in legends.
Anika Patel: Thanks everyone. Action items: Jamie — update Figma with Project-first default and toggle state memory; Matt — add ARIA snippets to the component doc; Sarah — finalize microcopy edits and accessibility checklist; I'll move invoice link to both places and wire up the export copy.
ui-bot: Added reaction :thumbsup: to Anika's message and attached updated Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/XXX/usage-dashboard-v3
Jamie Chen: Quick design question follow-up — should the org/project breadcrumb be clickable for power users? I think yes, low cost to implement.
Matt O'Neill: Clickable breadcrumbs are fine. Ensure focusable and provide title attribute on hover.
Sarah Lopez: And include skip link: "Skip to usage charts" at the top for keyboard users.
Anika Patel: Perfect — I'll schedule a 20-min sync for tomorrow to finalize. Thanks :sparkles:
